title: Russian Doll Envelopes
question: Why are equal-width envelopes sorted by descending height?
answer: The height LIS must not select two envelopes with the same width. Sorting tied widths in descending height prevents them from appearing as an increasing height subsequence.

title: Russian Doll Envelopes
question: What does tails store in the LIS phase?
answer: tails[i] is the smallest possible ending height of an increasing chain of length i+1. Replacing the first tail not smaller than a height preserves the best future extension options.

title: Count Numbers with Unique Digits
question: How many choices are available for each digit of a unique-digit number?
answer: The first digit of a multi-digit number has nine nonzero choices. The next digit has nine unused choices, then eight, and so on as used digits are excluded.

title: Count Numbers with Unique Digits
question: Why does the count stop increasing after ten digits?
answer: There are only ten decimal digits, so a number with all distinct digits cannot have more than ten positions. Longer lengths add no new valid numbers.

title: Largest Divisible Subset
question: Why is sorting helpful for the divisible-subset DP?
answer: For positive values, if a smaller value divides a larger value, the smaller appears earlier after sorting. The DP can therefore extend chains from earlier indices.

title: Largest Divisible Subset
question: How does the predecessor array reconstruct the subset?
answer: The algorithm records the prior index whenever a longer chain is found. Starting from the endpoint with the largest DP length and following those links recovers the subset in reverse.

title: Wiggle Subsequence
question: What do the up and down states represent?
answer: up is the best subsequence length ending with a rise, and down is the best length ending with a fall. A new rise extends down, while a new fall extends up.

title: Wiggle Subsequence
question: Why are equal adjacent values ignored?
answer: A wiggle requires strictly positive and negative differences alternating. A zero difference is neither direction and cannot extend either state.

title: Combination Sum IV
question: Why does the outer loop iterate over totals rather than numbers?
answer: The task counts ordered sequences, so each total considers every possible final number. This allows different orders of the same numbers to count as distinct sequences.

title: Combination Sum IV
question: What does dp[0]=1 represent?
answer: There is one way to make total zero: choose no numbers. That base case lets a number equal to the current total contribute one sequence.

title: Kth Smallest Element in a Sorted Matrix
question: How does value-domain binary search locate the kth smallest value?
answer: For each midpoint, count entries no greater than it. If the count is below k, the answer is larger; otherwise the answer is at most the midpoint.

title: Kth Smallest Element in a Sorted Matrix
question: Why can the matrix count be done in linear time?
answer: Starting at the bottom-left, each move either removes one row from consideration or accounts for a column segment and moves right. Each pointer moves at most n steps.

title: Insert Delete GetRandom O(1)
question: Why does removal swap in the last array element?
answer: Removing an arbitrary array position would shift later elements and cost O(n). Moving the last element into the gap and updating its map index keeps removal average O(1).

title: Insert Delete GetRandom O(1)
question: Why is random selection uniform in the array-plus-map design?
answer: Each stored value occupies exactly one array position, and getRandom chooses a uniformly random index. Thus every present value has equal probability.

title: Insert Delete GetRandom O(1) - Duplicates allowed
question: Why must each value map to a set of indices?
answer: A value can occupy several array positions. The set records every occurrence so removing one copy can select an index and repair the array after swapping.

title: Insert Delete GetRandom O(1) - Duplicates allowed
question: How does the implementation handle removing the final array position?
answer: It removes that index from the value's set, then performs the swap-and-delete bookkeeping. When the removed slot is already the last position, the final set update cancels the temporary reinsert.

title: Ransom Note
question: Why is a frequency counter enough to test ransom-note construction?
answer: The only constraint is whether each required letter has enough copies. Counting available magazine letters and decrementing on use detects shortages immediately.

title: Ransom Note
question: What is the complexity when the alphabet is fixed to lowercase English letters?
answer: Time is O(n+m) for scanning the two strings. The 26-element counter uses O(1) auxiliary space because the alphabet size is fixed.

title: Lexicographical Numbers
question: How does the prefix-tree view produce lexicographical order?
answer: A number is visited before its extensions, and its children are formed by appending digits 0 through 9. This matches dictionary ordering of decimal strings.

title: Lexicographical Numbers
question: When does the traversal backtrack instead of descending?
answer: If curr*10 exceeds n, it cannot descend. It then moves to the next sibling, first stripping trailing nines or prefixes whose next sibling would exceed n.
